facets.F1_correctness: SearchIndexRebuildPlan validates distinct active and rebuild index names, requires a replay source cursor, preserves tenant and cell scope, and bounds rebuild batch size.
facets.F2_tests: Buck2 unit tests cover the rollback-safe index split, tenant/cell scope, empty cursor rejection, same-index rejection, max batch clamp, and default batch size.
facets.F3_maintainability: The contract stays in the provider-neutral office search kernel; adapters can implement OpenSearch, Meilisearch, Tantivy, or owned search backends without coupling the kernel to a provider SDK.
facets.F4_compatibility: The change is additive and does not alter DriveSearchDocument, DriveSearchQuery, SearchIndexName, Buck targets, Cargo manifests, or generated artifacts.
facets.F5_security: No credentials, unsafe Rust, network calls, shell execution, or provider privileges are introduced. Rebuild inputs are validated before adapter execution.
facets.F6_privacy: No user content processing is added. The source cursor is an opaque checkpoint string and search documents remain data-class aware and redacted.
facets.F7_operability: The active index remains untouched until an adapter explicitly switches over, which gives operators a rollback-safe rebuild path.
facets.F8_performance: Batch size is bounded with an explicit default and maximum so adapters cannot accidentally request an unbounded replay batch.
facets.F9_compliance: No hand-edited *.generated.json files and no new dependencies. New SearchIndexRebuildPlan kernel fields carry inline data_class annotations. The evidence artifact follows the existing 2.4-compatible multispectrum shape used in this checkout.
facets.F10_reversibility: Rollback is a normal git revert of one Rust contract file and this evidence file; no data migration or production state mutation is introduced.
facets.F11_observability: The rebuild plan exposes tenant_id, cell_id, source_cursor, active_index_name, rebuild_index_name, and batch_size so future adapters can emit audit and progress events without parsing provider-specific state.
facets.F13_migration: Moves office search toward owned-stack migration by declaring the lifecycle seam before adopting any provider-specific search adapter.
facets.M1_challenge_assumption: Rejected provider-first index lifecycle design; the kernel owns the minimal replay and rollback contract while adapters remain replaceable.
facets.M2_zoomed_out_fit: This closes a narrow red/yellow hyperscaler gap without touching shared hot files, generated faces, or cross-domain contracts.
